citeAs: Bai, Yushi, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, and Juanzi Li. (2023). LongBench: A Bilingual, Multitask Benchmark for Long Context Understanding. arXiv.
creator: Yushi Bai, Xin Lv, Jiajie Zhang, Hongchang Lyu, Jiankai Tang, Zhidian Huang, Zhengxiao Du, Xiao Liu, Aohan Zeng, Lei Hou, Yuxiao Dong, Jie Tang, Juanzi Li (Tsinghua University; Zhipu.AI; Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences)
description: LongBench is a bilingual, multi-task benchmark for long context understanding. It comprises 21 datasets across 6 task categories in English and Chinese, standardized into a unified format for automatic evaluation of large language models on long-context tasks.
name: LongBench
publisher: Tsinghua University, Zhipu.AI, Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
rai:annotationsPerItem: For MultiFieldQA, three Ph.D. students were invited to annotate the question and answer for each article.
rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators for MultiFieldQA were Ph.D. students with extensive research experience in NLP, described as expert annotators.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For MultiFieldQA, cross-validation among annotators showed a 100% accuracy rate of the annotated answers. The average time taken to annotate each sample was around 5 minutes.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For the manually created MultiFieldQA datasets, the authors invited three Ph.D. students to annotate one question and a ground-truth answer for each document. Annotation guidelines required questions to be clear, have definitive and relatively short answers, vary in type, and have evidence distributed as randomly as possible throughout the article. The annotators also ensured that answers could be inferred from the documents.
rai:dataBiases: The authors state that during MultiFieldQA annotation they ensured that evidence placement was fairly random to avoid biases such as answer-related statements frequently appearing at the beginning or end of documents.
rai:dataCollection: LongBench is composed of 21 datasets across 6 task categories. Six datasets are directly extracted from original datasets, ten are built based on original datasets and processed for long-context evaluation, and five are created and annotated by the authors. Collection sources include literature, film, scientific papers, legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, Wikipedia, Baidu Search, meetings, news, dialogues, web questions, C4, and GitHub repositories.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw/source data come from original public datasets and source corpora such as long stories, NLP papers, legal documents, government reports, encyclopedias, Wikipedia passages, Baidu Search and Baidu Zhidao documents, meeting transcripts, news articles, dialogues, C4 Chinese sections, and GitHub code repositories.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Document analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The paper states two limitations: automatic metrics such as ROUGE-L and F1 may not accurately reflect response quality, and performance on LongBench is coupled with models' instruction-following capabilities rather than isolating long-context modeling alone.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The benchmark data are manipulated after collection to suit long-context evaluation. Examples include adding distracting passages until a maximum length is reached, randomly ordering passages in multi-document QA, randomly selecting and concatenating few-shot training examples into the context, shuffling synthetic-task passages, repeating paragraphs at random in PassageCount, selecting one passage for GPT-3.5-Turbo summarization in PassageRetrieval, and shuffling cross-file code snippets in RepoBench-P.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: All 21 datasets are standardized into a unified format. Additional preprocessing includes extracting long-document instances, sampling from original datasets, adapting datasets to long-context evaluation by concatenating documents or passages, adding distracting passages, randomly ordering passages, selecting long segments, filtering TriviaQA passages with fewer than 1,000 words as examples, and shuffling cross-file code snippets for RepoBench-P.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating long context understanding abilities of large language models across six task categories: single-document QA, multi-document QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code completion. It is also intended as a benchmark for future research in long context modeling.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5-Turbo is used in the synthetic PassageRetrieval tasks to summarize one selected passage and create the query abstract.
